item.title: Re: whats otaku and furry??
item.content:encoded:
I know this is an old thread; but I couldn't just leave this misconception uncorrected here.

Furry is not a sexual thing; to be a furry just means that you're interested in stuff related to characters with both human and animal characteristics, artwork, stories etc. Rule 34 is a thing though.

When referring to people, "furry" is actually short for "furry fan"; just like how there are sci-fi fans, western fans etc. But when referring to characters and such, "furry" means zooanthropomorphic, in broad terms, characters that have both animal and human characteristics (can be anything from body parts, to behaviors, instincts, intelligence etc. But regarding the intelligence part, that usually leans strongly towards human; it's extremely rare for a furry character to not be a "person" in this regard, regardless of what type of body they have).

Furries have a tendency to have a lot of furry-specific words, both for stuff that already have normal words for as well as some furry specific terms; the relevant example being Rule 34; furry Rule 34 is referred to as "yiff" (a word that also serves as a stand-in for "sex" and some other sex related terms). In more recent times though, that has become a lot more diluted; some old terms have stuck, but others have faded away and there aren't too many new ones getting widely used. But in recent years bronies (fans of the higher-quality reboot of the My Little Pony franchise, My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic) seem to have resurrected the practice, creating many terms specific for their subfandom; including their equivalent to "yiff", "clop" (though, while "yiff" refers to sex, "clop" refers to masturbation; but when used as an adjective to artwork, stories etc, it has the same meaning, it means it's Rule 34).

item.title: Different interpretation
item.content:encoded:
They're feeding her liver (not human) because it's the favourite meal of many wild animals. There's meat, then there are innards and wild animals usually go straight for the innards if given the chance, specifically liver, heart and lungs. Anyway, my take on this.

+ show block
– hide block

953 escaped. She spent some time hiding, learning about humans, planning… She's mischievous "spirit", wild one. It's all about the thrill of the hunt for her, of deception, of… being better than humans. Then she went to the convention to test her skills. And she did. And she was successful for the first victim. And she was successful in tricking and killing the second victim. And again. And again. And it started to become too easy. So she did it again. So she tried killing those people different ways. And she was successful. And again. And again. And again. In the end, when Foundation came to apprehend her, she just surrendered. I imagine it went like this.
953 is sitting on a bar stool with a stiff drink in front of her, staring in the middle distance, not looking at anything in particular; a thousand yard stare surrounded by blood, covered by blood, just staring. Foundation personnel is bursting in there, heavily armed, pointing guns at her.
953 sighs, gives bored shrug, thinks something like "Here's more of them. Gah." turns to face them and says something like.
"Just… Just take me away. This… this is not fun any more. Just… *shrug, sad shake of the head* just take me back to my cell. I… I've got nothing. *shakes head, spreads and waves arms and tails in bored frustration* Nothing! Just… *sigh* nothing." *almost starts crying, thinking 'Ye gods, why is this game so boring! What am I going to do now?! I fulfilled all my fantasies! I did everything I wanted to try ever! I did everything I planned for years! So why am I feeling so empty inside?!'*

Be careful what you wish for.

Sort of like playing a RPG game, gaining levels, finishing the main quest then returning to the starting areas and slaughtering enemies that gave you trouble 40+ levels ago, from the weakest to the strongest, you kill them all in one hit, you do it for two hours, you kill them with gleeful abandon and it's cathartic, you get the release you want then… you get bored. You go to slightly stronger enemies, kill them too, then you try using the unusual weapons which you couldn't use during main quest because enemies were too strong when you got those weapons but they are not too strong now! And some of those weapons and magics are really fun, now there's no chance of your character getting hurt. Then you use up all your different weapons and all the ways you get to kill those enemies, you see all the animations, all easter eggs, and killing things, no matter how strong, no matter what way you kill them, it starts to feel the same and you get bored of the game for good. That's the moment you stop playing.

It feels like she went to the convention, felt like using God Mode in the video game (I mean, even her disadvantages of showing ears, tail or weird eyes would go unnoticed on that sort of convention) then got bored of killing and tricking humans for good. So she stopped playing.

Please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.content:encoded:
1. SCP 953 is hostile because she is a fox demon. Kumiho in general are malicious beings, whose legend typically describes them as being bloodthirsty. SCP 953 displays a pattern of sociopathic behavior (and basically seems to lack a conscience). So she doesn't care who you are, if you are a threat to her: you're done. If she feels insulted by you: you're done. If she sees you as her meal: you're done. Not to mention that she enjoys inflicting pain, so she is also sadistic. Basically; she is evil, so she is going to do evil shit. It's in her nature. She only "cares" about how humans view her because it allows her to hide under her mask of beauty and harmlessness while she is ripping out your liver. It's all apart of what makes her a trickster. Once she knows that you know what she is, her true nature can surface.

You're forgetting that what Ihpkmn stated is only one variation of the Kumiho legend. Some tales states that Kumiho eat hearts, not liver. Some tales say that if a Kumiho abstains from killing and eating humans for a thousand days, it can become human. One version of the mythology, states holds that with enough will, a Kumiho could further ascend from its yokwe (monster) state and become permanently human and lose its evil character. Because there are so many differing varations of the Kumiho, DrClef cannot be too specific, and so Clef is forced to go with the general description of the Kumiho mythology: that Kumiho are evil foxes that appear as beautiful women to seduce men and eat their flesh. Calling an error because SCP 953 doesn't follow a specific lore is illogical when you're dealing with a legend that has many different variations and constantly changes throughout history.

I'm not sure a demon fox can have a "tragic past", but I can agree that we could use alittle more insight of what she did before she was captured.

2. Calling a Kumiho a Kitsune is like calling a Korean person Japanese. Most people will correct you if they understand that you made a mistake, some people would be offended. Now once again, remembering the fact this is an evil, malicious, sociopathic demon fox; this is probably wouldn't sit well with someone like her.

Not to mention the fact that despite the Kumiho and the Kitsune both being 9 tailed foxes, they are almost polar opposites; they may be the same legend/myth but they aren't exactly the same creature. So having people confuse SCP 953 with a Kitsune wouldn't do the article any good, and would actually look extremely contradictory when you compare Kitsune legend to SCP 953.

4. Ehh, I dont think the addenda is THAT bad, but then again, this is purely opinion.

item.content:encoded:
Man, even years after reading this article 953 still tugs at my heartstrings.

Though this is one of the older and more popular SCPs I feel like there's a few changes that could help wrap this thing up and make it concrete. A few of the things that bother me:

-Nowhere in either the main article or the attached interview are there any real hints as to why 953 is so damn hostile. Most of the time hyper-aggressive SCPs like this have either a reason to kill people or they're specifically designed to draw their horror aspect from murdering everything they see (ie, 682 and 76). 953 is clearly very intelligent and cares quite a bit about how humans view her.

Killing people to become human makes sense, but as stated almost 2 years ago by Ihpkmn, the particular legend that deals with that concept says that they have to consume the flesh of 1000 humans in 1000 years and that Kumiho often gain a tail per 100 years. There's no way that 953 hasn't killed 1000 people in over 900 years, considering that she killed over ██ in ██ years.

Her current backstory is already pretty depressing and there's so much potential to make it even better by giving us a bit of insight on her (presumably) tragic past if her goal isn't just KILL ALL HUMAN, 4noraisin.

-Kumiho and Kitsune are two sides of the same coin. They're just different interpretations of the same legend by different cultures. I don't see why 953 would violently lash out at this since they're labels being applied by humans and not by their own species anyways. As intelligent as she is, getting mad at that is just dumb.

-Some of the addenda are cringeworthy. They really need to be completely wiped and rewritten along with the help of an actual furry and/or weeaboo. Right now it's like watching Fox News talk about internet culture. I'm not saying the addenda and their implications should be removed entirely. Their purpose is fine and they hit pretty hard, especially against people who start to sympathize with 953 just because it can turn into a cute girl.

I'm not really that into the SCP community so I don't know if Clef is even alive, let alone if this comment will get to him. Hopefully it does but I just wanted to throw all this out here anyways.

item.content:encoded:
Hey kids! It's time for Myth Time with Uncle Ihp!

Did you know that Kumiho gain more tails as they age? Kumiho can have up to nine tails, each tail growing over the course of 100 years, Since 953 is a full nine-tailed Kumiho, we can assume that she's 800-900 years old, assuming she had one tail when she was born.

Secondly, the main goal in a Kumiho's life is to turn into a human. They do this by consuming human flesh; according to Korean culture, at one time, humans were considered only one step below the gods. So, foxes ate human flesh, primarily the liver, in order to become more human. It can do this by eating 1000 livers in 1000 years, otherwise, it'll dissolve into bubbles. Since it's over 800 years old, and still hasn't become human… it's kind of sucking at its job. Seriously, how many furries did she kill without eating their livers? What a waste.

Other myths state that kumiho become human by not killing humans for 1000 days, or roughly 32 months. I'm assuming that 953 has been in containment for longer than that, and since she hasn't become human yet, she's probably killed quite a few agents or this isn't that kind of Kumiho.

This has been Myth Time with Uncle Ihp.

*removes the Sarcasm hat*

In all seriousness, I just now realize the wasted potential this article has. This creature wants to be human, and she could've been juxtaposed against humans who want to be animals, instead of just blindly killing them because they made porn of her and her kind. And I still can't figure out why the flim-flam this thing is Keter. It's a shapeshifting fox, yes, but why is it Keter? Are they afraid that it'll exterminate every furry and otaku in the world? I can tell you that wouldn't be a very big loss.

So, I've changed my upvote to a downvote.
